recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Adding more HTTP-local wording would duplicate the current search-page source of truth and run counter to the later FHIR-36347 cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-8234 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 FHIR-core HTTP search issue asking what "the standard search parameters" meant when searching all resources at once, especially whether `_text`, `_content`, `_query`, and `_filter` were included and whether `_query` could be used at system level.
initial_application: The issue was applied by commit 18b42d91ae86b341b60128cf1bffd666879df42d, the git-svn mirror of SVN revision 5347, which linked HTTP all-resource search to the all-resource parameter list and updated the search page to include `_content` and `_query` while documenting `_filter` as a special search parameter.
additional_context: Later final search decisions refined the same area without reversing the seed: FHIR-12985 added `_type` to all-resource parameters, FHIR-13836 clarified the `_type`/all-types rule, FHIR-36347 centralized the detailed parameter-availability rules on the search page, and FHIR-42911 removed duplicate `_text`/`_filter` prose.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current `source/search.html` states that base searches without `_type` use parameters common to all resource types, explains the multi-type `_type` case, and lists all-resource parameters including `_content`, `_filter`, `_query`, `_type`, and `_text`; current `source/http.html` links to that maintained search-page section.

related_jiras.note: Added `_type` to the all-resource search parameter family after FHIR-8234.
Clarified that `_type` determines whether non-`_type` parameters must be common to selected types or all resource types.
Moved detailed multiple-type and all-type search parameter guidance from the HTTP page into the search page.
Removed duplicate all-resources prose once `_text` and `_filter` were already listed.
